evidence.requirements: Nearly every requirement is met. The list has the heading, name links, family and L3, the Search field, the Family select and the '<n> cartridges' count (index.html:13-32, app.js:11-27). Search ignores spaces, so '7,62 x 51' finds 308 Win. (format.js:69-72). The detail view shows every fact listed in the brief plus the capacity source link (app.js:50-56). Tables are grouped by section with Symbol/Value/Unit columns (app.js:38-42). Tolerances are folded into the value (format.js:41-45). Angles show as 40° or 39°59'49". Hash routes survive a reload. Print button and back link are present. The SVG has role=img and the name '<name> drawing'. All required dimensions are drawn (drawing.js:132-204). The title block shows name, table, revision date, 'Dimensions in mm' and the scale. Missing values are listed in a figcaption (app.js:58). Partly met: (1) in print the table headers are hidden (style.css:107), so the printed tables lose their Symbol/Value/Unit columns; (2) the fillet radius is silently reduced when r1 min or r2 does not fit (geometry.js:39-43; affects 6,5 x 55 with r1 min 3.5 and 7,62 x 39 with r1 min 4.0), so the drawn radius differs from the published one and no note says so; (3) on the heeled 22 Long Rifle the outside view draws no line at the mouth, so case and bullet merge (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg); the reference shows the mouth.
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules closely. Chamfer: R1/2 - min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (geometry.js:146). Rimfire half-round radius min(R/2, (R1-P1)/2) with its outermost point at R1/2. Groove floor and ramp, and the belt ramp at δ to R3/2 (geometry.js:166-178). Shoulder through the published points. Seating, k factors and meplats per shape and category (geometry.js:14-19, 231-236). Correct tangent ogive centre (bulletOutline). Heeled bullet uses H2 and H2-2tb. Walls follow the tb/tn formulas with a linear blend across the shoulder. w follows the max rule. Primer pocket table is correct, and the pocket is cut out of the hatch (geometry.js:262-263). Screenshots match the references in outline and proportion (308, 300 WM, 9 mm, 22 LR); the semi-wadcutter cone is visible on 44 Rem. Mag. and the shallow 10°58' shoulder on 9,3 x 74 R. Label values match the data, and print-308_win.jpg is one A4 page. Faults: the right-hand diameter extension lines run horizontally along the body and through the bullet. P1's line lies about 0.2 mm from the tapered body, so the outline looks doubled (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-300_win_mag.jpg). The α arc is tiny and barely readable on shallow shoulders (detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg). The heeled outside view has no mouth line. Fillets are clamped silently.
evidence.security: All data that reaches innerHTML goes through esc() (app.js:5, 12-13, 35-41, 47-62; drawing.js:15, 96, 218). There is no eval, Function or setTimeout with a string. No external requests: system fonts only, and no CDN (index.html). An e2e test asserts that only file:// URLs are requested (app.spec.js:191-202). The only outbound links are the user-clicked capacity sources, opened with rel=noopener.
evidence.code_quality: Clear split into data/format/geometry/drawing/app. Geometry and format are pure, DOM-free modules usable from Node. Rules map to commented blocks ('2. head face', '3. extractor groove'). Missing values are collected rather than invented. Weaknesses: dense one-liners (drawing.js:132-166, 196), esc() and has() duplicated with different semantics (drawing.js:18 vs geometry.js:8), bodyR re-implements interp (drawing.js:117-125 vs geometry.js:69-78), and a string placeholder @@SCALE@@ is used for the scale text. Size fits the task: about 250 lines each for geometry and drawing.
evidence.tests: node:test unit suites cover rim-type thresholds, the chamfer/groove/belt/rimfire points, fillets, ogive circle conformity, the quarter ellipse, seating and k factors per shape, the heeled bullet, walls and w, primer pockets, and the hatch excluding the pocket. They also check that labels and missing notes are not invented, and that no label overlaps another label, an outline or a line, for all 25 records (drawing.test.js:99-133). Playwright covers list/search/filter, reload and bookmark, facts, tables, units, DMS, the Print call, file:// and http serving, phone-width overflow, theme, one-page PDF for all 25 cartridges, and label point size in print. The last run passed (.last-run.json). Gaps: no test catches extension lines lying on the outline. Flat and semi-wadcutter cone outlines are not checked point by point. There is no visual check of the heeled mouth.
evidence.ux_design: Facts grid and dense tables suit a technical audience; tabular numbers, right-aligned values and a muted unit column work well (detail-308_win.jpg). The drawing is legible and labels don't collide. However, label size is fixed in mm, so short cartridges get huge text: 9 mm Luger at 4.7:1 and 22 LR at 5:1 have labels about 40 px tall and a title block larger than the page heading (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-22_long_rifle.jpg). Extension lines crossing the bullet and doubling the body outline clutter the profile. The α annotation is cramped. The print layout is compact and clean but drops the table headers (print-308_win.jpg). Dark mode exists in CSS (style.css:12-21); there is no screenshot of it.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img, aria-label and a <title> (drawing.js:236-237). Inputs are wrapped in <label> elements. The count uses role=status. Tables have a caption and th headers. Focus moves to the h1 on navigation (app.js:110). focus-visible outlines are defined (style.css:34). All controls are native, with lang=en. Contrast is adequate (muted #596066 on #fbfbf9). Minor: the list table has no caption, th has no scope, and 0.7rem table headers are small. The drawing alternative is only its name, though the tables carry every value.
evidence.simplicity: Plain HTML/CSS/JS with no runtime dependencies. Playwright 1.64.1 is the only dev dependency. Five small JS files, no build step, and data embedded in a script so file:// works. Proportionate to the problem.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, so no run or setup instructions. There is no CI pipeline, no ADRs, no changelog or release process (version 1.0.0 is never explained), and no engines/.nvmrc for Node 22. playwright.config.js:6-12 has an undocumented hack that searches the container's Chromium. Positives: three OpenSpec specs describe the behaviour (openspec/specs/*), package-lock.json pins the dev dependency, npm scripts are obvious, and the regression tests are broad.
evidence.visual_design: Calm palette, consistent spacing and small-caps section headings; it looks finished on the list and table pages (list.jpg, detail-308_win.jpg). The drawing's heavy monospace text clashes with the light UI, and its size varies wildly between cartridges because it is fixed in mm (9 mm and 22 LR versus 308). The title block dominates small cartridges. The print sheet is crisp black on white.
evidence.layout: The order is right: name, facts, drawing, tables, footer. The tables flow in a 4-column grid. No overlaps or clipping are visible. For short cartridges the drawing panel fills about 1000 px of height with mostly empty space and an oversized title block, pushing the tables far down (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-22_long_rifle.jpg). The R dimension leaves a large blank band. In print, everything fits one page with room to spare (print-308_win.jpg).
evidence.usability: One click from list to detail. Live filtering combines search and family. Filters are kept when returning via 'All cartridges' (tested in app.spec.js:80-89). Bookmarkable hash URLs. An unknown key shows 'Cartridge not found' with a back link. A 'No cartridge matches.' message appears. The Print button works. The list cannot be sorted, which is acceptable for 25 rows.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust the faithful values, tolerances and DMS angles, the true-scale section with primer pocket, and the one-page print. Oversized labels on pistol and rimfire drawings and the extension lines crossing the profile look less professional than the OpenBallistics references. A missing README would worry any contributor.

unmet_requirements: Printed tables hide their Symbol/Value/Unit column headers (style.css:107)
Shoulder fillet radii are silently reduced when r1 min/r2 do not fit (geometry.js:39-43); the drawn radius differs from the published value and no note says so
Heeled 22 Long Rifle outside view has no mouth line, so case and bullet are indistinguishable (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg)
Diameter extension lines run along the body outline and through the bullet, reducing drawing legibility (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-300_win_mag.jpg)
strengths: The geometry engine implements the brief's rules faithfully: chamfer, groove, belt ramp at δ, rimfire half-round, tangent ogive, heeled bullet, walls, w and primer pocket. Missing values are reported, never invented.
Broad, meaningful tests: unit checks of each rule, plus label-overlap and one-page-A4 checks for all 25 cartridges in Chromium.
Plain, dependency-free static app with consistent HTML escaping, no network requests, bookmarkable routes and a clean one-page black-on-white print.
issues: Drawing legibility: right-hand diameter extension lines run along the body and through the bullet, so the outline looks doubled. The α arc is tiny, and the heeled 22 LR has no visible mouth line.
Labels and the title block are fixed in mm, so short cartridges (9 mm Luger, 22 LR) render huge text and a mostly empty drawing panel, while the print tables drop their column headers.
Maintainability: no README, CI, ADRs, release notes or Node version pin, and an undocumented Chromium lookup hack in playwright.config.js.
review.verdict: A careful, well-tested implementation that draws all 25 cartridges true to scale from the brief's rules, with correct data formatting, safe rendering and a one-page A4 print. The drafting polish (extension lines over the profile, oversized labels on small cartridges, the missing heeled mouth line) and the lack of any README or CI keep it short of publishable as is.
